I drive a semi truck and have been using these systems for the last 5 years.

I hate them, especially when the volume is set at max by default. The system blast a horn on the side of the truck that crossed a line deafening the driver.
Is this the kind of shit I have to look forward to if I start doing OTR? Driving a '94 LTL9000 with a flowboy right now but paving sucks for winters.

Some of the older lane departure systems can be bypassed with a playing card in front of the sensor. We have newer systems at the company I'm at and we can't really do that.

There's also a Bendix system that'll make a noise if you're following too close to someone. There's a couple different models of this system. The first one I used would jab the brakes if you got too close to someone or if someone cut you off. It would also jab the brakes if you had to pull close to an object to set up for a back. Snow storms and heavy rain would also set it off which is dangerous for slippery conditions.

The one that's in my trucks now isn't that bad. It has a volume control which is nice, and works two different ways. If your cruise control is off it will just beep. If your cruise control is on it will have control of your brakes so if you're not using the cruise turn it off. When the cruise is on it will slow you down to a "safe distance" havent had any issues in bad conditions with it yet.

The only downside to the second unit is that I had one malfunction on me a couple months ago and shut my truck down in the middle of the highway. There was also a plastic bag that got stuck in front of it.

I'd avoid any company that has driver facing camera's though.
